For a %1$s child facing a tough online interaction, stay calm first so %2$s feels safe coming to you again:
• Validate before reacting: thank them for telling you and avoid immediately confiscating the phone as punishment.
• Capture evidence calmly: keep the redacted SafeNest alert and block the sender/platform together.
• Conversation starter: "I saw something that worried me — you're not in trouble. Can we look at it together and decide how to handle it?"

Practical screen-time plan for %1$s (%2$s, current limit %3$dm/day):
• Replace sudden cutoffs with predictable category caps (e.g., School Night preset: 30m Video, 30m Games, 20m Social).
• Give a 10-minute wrap-up cue before a match or episode ends to prevent meltdowns.
• Conversation starter: "You get to pick which 30 minutes of gaming feel best today — after homework or before dinner?"

Protecting sleep for %1$s (Bedtime %2$s–%3$s):
• Charge devices outside the bedroom 30 minutes before %2$s so bedtime feels like a family routine, not a punishment.
• Keep SafeNest DNS Shield + Bedtime Downtime active so late-night autoplay never restarts.
• Conversation starter: "Let's both park our phones in the kitchen at %2$s so we wake up sharp tomorrow."
